long_biography.plain_text:
Mark Denning helped organise an investment in Bank of Ireland when the lender was emerging from the financial crisis. Working with analyst Joerg Sponer at Capital Group, he helped assemble a deal with other investors that kept the bank from full nationalisation. The opportunity depended on looking beyond its losses to a more concentrated banking market, where the surviving lenders had greater pricing power.

Denning spent his first twenty years in Malaysia and worked as an investment analyst covering Southeast Asian companies. His stock selection combined a search for businesses that could improve over time with caution about the price paid for their earnings. In 2009, unusually low valuations prompted him to take more risk than he normally would.
long_biography.html:
Mark Denning helped organise an investment in Bank of Ireland when the lender was emerging from the financial crisis. Working with analyst Joerg Sponer at Capital Group, he helped assemble a deal with other investors that kept the bank from full nationalisation. The opportunity depended on looking beyond its losses to a more concentrated banking market, where the surviving lenders had greater pricing power.

Denning spent his first twenty years in Malaysia and worked as an investment analyst covering Southeast Asian companies. His stock selection combined a search for businesses that could improve over time with caution about the price paid for their earnings. In 2009, unusually low valuations prompted him to take more risk than he normally would.
